source: Hong and Page (2004) Groups of diverse problem solvers can outperform groups of high-ability problem solvers
finding: Agent model on a ring landscape. A group of randomly picked agents beat a group of the best-scoring agents. The best agents end up similar, so their joint search is narrow.
numbers: Table (collective score, diversity): 20 agents, l=12: best 93.78 (diversity 74.95) vs random 94.72 (91.46). 10 agents, l=20: best 93.52 (73.69) vs random 96.08 (94.31).
quote: a team of randomly selected agents outperforms a team comprised of the best-performing agents
limits: Simulation and theorem, no human data. Ability is measured on the same problem the group then solves. Needs a large pool and special conditions.
agent_relevance: For an ensemble of one model, diversity of method matters more than picking the top individual samples. Matches the case for varied prompts.

source: Hong and Page (2004), the theorem section
finding: The authors say the result is a proof under stated conditions, and the best group in the finite version is identical agents, an artifact of finiteness.
numbers: Conditions: problems hard, agents locally optimal, pool large, agent set diverse. In the general version best agents are similar, not identical.
quote: the group of the best-performing agents is proven below to be comprised of identical agents
limits: Later critics say these conditions rarely hold for real scientists (see b13).
agent_relevance: Do not read this as a law. It is conditional on a large, truly diverse candidate pool.

source: Hofstra et al. (2020) The diversity-innovation paradox in science
finding: Underrepresented groups introduce more novel concept links, but their novelty is taken up less and pays off less in careers.
numbers: About 1.2 million US PhDs 1977-2015. Underrepresented genders: about 5% lower odds of a faculty job, 6% lower odds of a sustained research career. Underrepresented races: 25% lower faculty odds, 10% lower career odds. At +2 SD novelty the faculty gap grows from about 3.5% (4.3%) to 9.5% (15%) for novelty (impactful novelty).
quote: underrepresented groups produce higher rates of scientific novelty. However, their novel contributions are devalued and discounted
limits: Observational. Novelty is a text-based measure (new links between concepts). Cannot separate bias from other causes.
agent_relevance: A diverse source of ideas is useless if the aggregator discounts it. For a pool of agent views, check the merge step does not down-weight minority views.

source: Yang, Tian, Woodruff, Jones, Uzzi (2022) Gender-diverse teams produce more novel and higher-impact scientific ideas
finding: Mixed-gender teams publish more novel and more cited medical papers than same-gender teams of equal size. Effect grows toward 50/50 balance.
numbers: 6.6 million papers since 2000. Large teams (more than 6 authors): 9.1% more likely to be novel (48% vs 44%) and 14.6% more likely to be top-5% cited (10.2% vs 8.9%). Mixed-gender teams are under-represented by up to 17% vs a null model.
quote: mixed-gender teams are 14.6% more likely to publish an upper-tail paper than same-gender teams of equal size
limits: Observational, gender inferred by algorithm. Holds with fixed effects for individuals and team structure, but not randomised.
agent_relevance: Large-scale support for a diversity benefit in discovery output. Effects are modest percent gains, not step changes.

source: Naik et al. (2023, v2 2024) Diversity of thought improves reasoning abilities of LLMs (DIV-SE)
finding: Asking the model for several different solution approaches, then ensembling, beats chain of thought and self-consistency on hard tasks and costs less.
numbers: GPT-4 Blocksworld 3: zero-shot CoT 15%, SC-10 23%, in-call variant (IDIV-SE) +59 points over CoT, DIV-SE 97%. Blocksworld 4/5: +29.6 points. About 4x lower cost than SC-10 in the few-shot setting.
quote: linguistic token diversity does not always ensure diverse and independent solution approaches
limits: Planning and graph colouring, with an external verifier for some runs. Error can propagate when approaches are chained in one call.
agent_relevance: Direct support: diverse methods, not just diverse tokens, is the useful diversity. Fits operators that generate rival approaches before committing.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Mixture-of-Agents enhances LLM capabilities
finding: Layered ensemble of different LLMs, aggregated by a final model, beat GPT-4o using only open models.
numbers: AlpacaEval 2.0 length-controlled win rate 65.1% vs 57.5% for GPT-4o (+7.6). MoA-Lite 59.3%. Runs repeated three times, mean and SD reported.
quote: multiple different LLMs consistently yielded better results
limits: Judge is a model (GPT-4 based). Win rate is not ground truth. Scores depend on aggregator choice.
agent_relevance: Evidence that a mix of models adds value beyond one strong model. A single-agent scaffold can mimic it with varied personas but gets less independence.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Mixture-of-Agents, ablation on model diversity
finding: Different models as proposers beat the same model sampled repeatedly, at every n above 1.
numbers: AlpacaEval 2.0 LC win rate, Qwen1.5-110B aggregator: n=6 multiple-proposer 61.3% vs single-proposer 56.7%; n=3 58.0 vs 56.1; n=2 58.8 vs 54.5; n=1 47.8 for both. Aggregator and proposer roles differ: Llama-3-70B scores 45.0% as aggregator but 60.6% as proposer.
limits: One benchmark, one aggregator. Gap is 2 to 5 points.
agent_relevance: Quantifies the diversity benefit as 2 to 5 points of win rate. Also: a good proposer is not a good aggregator, echoing ability vs diversity.

source: Jiang et al. (2025) Artificial Hivemind: the open-ended homogeneity of language models
finding: Models repeat themselves, and different model families also give near-identical open-ended answers. Real cognitive diversity across LLMs is thin.
numbers: INFINITY-CHAT: 26K real open-ended queries, 70+ models, 31,250 human labels (25 raters per item). Same model, 50 samples at top-p 0.9, T=1.0: in 79% of cases mean pairwise similarity above 0.8. Across models: 71% to 82% average similarity; DeepSeek-V3 vs qwen-max 0.82, vs gpt-4o 0.81. With min-p, 81% of pairs still above 0.7.
quote: different models produce strikingly similar outputs
limits: Similarity from one embedding model (text-embedding-3-small). Open-ended generation, not reasoning accuracy.
agent_relevance: Warns that Hong-Page style gains need real independence. Many LLM copies, even from many brands, may be one voice. Use method and framing diversity, not temperature.

source: Smit et al. (2023/2024) Should we be going MAD? A look at multi-agent debate strategies
finding: Debate between agents does not reliably beat self-consistency or ensembling. It is sensitive to settings. Tuning how much the agents agree at the start helps.
numbers: Benchmarked MedQA, PubMedQA, MMLU, CosmosQA and others. Multi-Persona debate scored about 0.58 on one dataset untuned; tuned agreement modulation lifted several MAD systems above non-debate baselines. Only part of the table was read.
quote: multi-agent debating systems, in their current form, do not reliably outperform other proposed prompting strategies
limits: Benchmarks are multiple-choice QA. Hyperparameter sensitivity makes comparison fragile.
agent_relevance: A failed replication of the idea that talking helps. Independent voting beats social exchange unless disagreement is managed.

source: Liang et al. (2023) Encouraging divergent thinking in LLMs through multi-agent debate
finding: Self-reflection gets stuck on its first answer (degeneration of thought). Debate with a judge breaks this. GPT-3.5 with MAD passed GPT-4 on Common MT.
numbers: Tasks: Common MT and Counter-Intuitive AR. Self-reflection shows low disagreement between rounds across 5 forced rounds. Exact accuracy table not re-read here.
limits: Small task set. Later work (b09) did not find debate reliably better.
agent_relevance: A single agent cannot easily produce a rival view of itself. Supports forced counter-position steps.

source: Li et al. (2024) More agents is all you need
finding: Plain sampling and majority vote over more copies raises accuracy. Gain grows with task difficulty. Smaller models scale to match bigger ones.
numbers: Gains from larger ensemble: GSM8K 12% to 24%, MATH 6% to 10%, HumanEval 4% to 9%. Llama2-13B at ensemble 15 matches Llama2-70B; Llama2-70B and GPT-3.5-Turbo comparable at 15 and 20. Ensemble up to 40.
limits: Copies are the same model, so errors correlate. Gains saturate.
agent_relevance: Baseline: quantity of independent samples gives gains without social interaction. Compare any diversity scaffold against this.

source: Cemri et al. (2025) Why do multi-agent LLM systems fail?
finding: Multi-agent systems fail often, mostly from design, agent misalignment and weak verification, not from model weakness alone.
numbers: MAST-Data: 1642 annotated traces, 7 frameworks, GPT-4 and Claude families. Failure rate 41% to 86.7%. 14 failure modes in 3 categories, annotator agreement kappa 0.88 on 150 traces. Disobey task specification 11.8% of traces.
limits: Open-source frameworks, specific task suites.
agent_relevance: Boundary condition: collective structure adds failure modes. A single-agent scaffold avoids inter-agent misalignment.

source: Thompson (2014) Can diversity trump ability? Critique of Hong and Page
finding: Recalled, not opened: argues the Hong-Page result holds only when the best group is drawn from an unrealistically small set of agents and ability is independent of diversity. In realistic settings ability matters.
numbers: No numbers recorded.
limits: Not verified this session; check before citing.
agent_relevance: Treat Hong-Page as conditional.

source: Grim, Singer, Bramson et al. (2019) Diversity, ability, and expertise in epistemic communities
finding: Recalled, not opened: re-ran Hong-Page style models on other landscapes. Reported the diversity advantage is not robust and often tracks ability.
numbers: No numbers recorded.
limits: Not verified.
agent_relevance: Warns against claiming diversity always trumps ability.

source: Weisberg and Muldoon (2009) Epistemic landscapes and the division of cognitive labor
finding: Agent model on a landscape. Followers copy others' findings, mavericks avoid trodden ground. Mixed populations did best, per the search abstract. Page returned 403.
numbers: No numbers recorded.
limits: Abstract only, via a search snippet.
agent_relevance: Supports explicit maverick roles in an ensemble.

source: Alexander, Himmelreich, Thompson (2015) Epistemic landscapes, optimal search, and the division of cognitive labor
finding: Recalled, not opened (fetch failed): a reply to Weisberg-Muldoon, reported to show the maverick advantage depends on model details.
numbers: None.
limits: Unverified details.
agent_relevance: Failed-replication style warning for landscape models.

source: Zollman (2010) The epistemic benefit of transient diversity
finding: Recalled, not opened: in a bandit-style network model, less connected networks reach the right theory more often because they keep diverse views longer.
numbers: None recorded.
limits: Not verified.
agent_relevance: Argues for delaying sharing between agents before merging.

source: Woolley et al. (2010) Evidence for a collective intelligence factor
finding: Recalled, not opened: group performance across tasks shows one factor c, tied to social sensitivity, equal turn-taking and proportion of women, not to average or max member IQ.
numbers: 699 people in 192 groups of 2 to 5 (from memory).
limits: Link to cognitive diversity is indirect.
agent_relevance: Group quality depends on process, not top-member ability.

source: Horwitz and Horwitz (2007) Effect of team diversity on team outcomes (meta-analysis)
finding: Recalled, not opened: task-related diversity (skills, education) relates positively to team performance; bio-demographic diversity does not.
numbers: About 35 studies (from memory).
limits: Effects small. Not verified.
agent_relevance: Functional diversity, not demographic labels, carries the benefit.

source: Stasser and Titus (1985) Pooling of unshared information in group decision making
finding: Recalled, not opened: groups discuss shared information more than unique information and so miss the best choice (hidden profile).
numbers: None recorded.
limits: Not verified.
agent_relevance: Diverse knowledge helps only if unshared items are surfaced. Collect each agent's unique evidence explicitly.

source: Longino (1990) Science as Social Knowledge
finding: Not opened: objectivity comes from public venues, uptake of criticism, shared standards and tempered equality.
numbers: None.
limits: Philosophical argument, no data.
agent_relevance: A checklist: open critique and responsiveness to it.

source: Fazelpour and Steel (2022) Diversity, trust, and conformity: a simulation study
finding: Recalled, not opened: simulation where diversity helps only if trust across groups is high enough; low trust or conformity pressure erases the gain.
numbers: None.
limits: Not verified.
agent_relevance: Boundary condition: the diversity benefit needs uptake.

source: Levine et al. (2014) Ethnic diversity deflates price bubbles
finding: Recalled, not opened: experimental markets with ethnically diverse traders priced more accurately and had smaller bubbles.
numbers: No numbers recorded.
limits: Not verified.
agent_relevance: Diverse skepticism lowers herding.

source: AlShebli, Rahwan, Woon (2018) The preeminence of ethnic diversity in scientific collaboration
finding: Recalled, not opened: papers with ethnically diverse author sets get more citations in large bibliographic data.
numbers: No numbers recorded.
limits: Observational.
agent_relevance: Another observational support.

source: Page (2007) The Difference
finding: Recalled, not opened: diversity prediction theorem. Collective squared error equals average individual error minus prediction diversity.
numbers: Identity: crowd error = mean individual error - prediction diversity.
limits: Holds for squared-error averaging only.
agent_relevance: Gives an exact quantity to track in an ensemble.
